events.region: SW Kenai Peninsula; NW Kenai Peninsula; Skilak Lake
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulations up to
3 inches and ice accumulations up to one tenth of an inch. Winds
gusting as high as 45 mph, mainly along the Inlet.

* WHERE...NW Kenai Peninsula, SW Kenai Peninsula, and Skilak Lake.

* WHEN...Until noon AKST today.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Along the coast, gusty winds
could bring down a few tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges
and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous overnight
into early Tuesday morning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas of light snow will transition to
freezing rain before becoming all rain with above freezing
temperatures Tuesday morning. There is increased confidence in a
quicker warm-up, meaning less snow accumulation and a quicker
changeover to rain. Areas at sea level will likely see little snow
accumulation, with most of the accumulation expected at higher
elevations, including the Homer Bluffs.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Total snow accumulation less
than 1 inch. Ice accumulations of a light glaze to a few hundredths
of an inch. Northeast winds gusting as high as 50 mph across parts
of the Matanuska Valley.

* WHERE...Anchorage and Lower Matanuska Valley.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM AKST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Across the Matanuska Valley,
gusty winds could bring down a few tree branches. Some roads and
bridges will likely become slick and hazardous, especially in wind
sheltered areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas of light snow will transition to
freezing rain before becoming all rain with above freezing
temperatures Tuesday morning. There is increased confidence in a
quicker warm-up, meaning less snow accumulation and a quicker
changeover to rain. Wind sheltered areas from east Anchorage up the
Glenn Highway to Eagle River, Chugiak, Eklutna, and the Butte will
hold on to freezing surface temperatures the longest, so roads
could be icy for the morning commute.

grouped_sources.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Mixed precipitation likely. Total snow accumulations between
4 and 12 inches. Ice accumulations around a light glaze possible.

* WHERE...Interior Kenai Peninsula and Turnagain Pass.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM AKST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Visibility could be
significantly reduced within heavy snow. Ponding of water along the
Seward Highway is likely due to rain and melting snow Tuesday
morning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A wintry mix of precipitation is expected to
persist for Turnagain Pass, Hope Cutoff, and Summit Lake areas
through early to mid morning before changing to rain. Valley
locations, including Tern Lake to Moose Pass will see lower snow
accumulation and a quicker transition from snow to rain. Rain on
top of snow that has already fallen may also lead to slush and
ponding for water on roads.

events.region: Sutton / Upper Matanuska Valley; Eureka / Tahneta Pass
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 4 and 8
inches.

* WHERE...Glenn Highway from Mile Post 90 to 150, including Eureka
and Tahneta Pass.

* WHEN...Until 11 AM AKST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Visibility could be
significantly reduced due to heavier snow and gusty winds.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Steady snow will continue through Tuesday
morning before tapering off. Snow may be heavy at times through 7
AM Tuesday. Winds may gust to around 20 mph times resulting in
localized areas of drifting snow.

temperatures Tuesday morning. There is increased confidence in a
quicker warm-up, meaning less snow accumulation and a quicker
changeover to rain.

events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall that has occurred upstream has resulted in river
levels just below Moderate flood stage. River levels are expected to
remain steady near Moderate Flood stage through this week and into
the weekend as a large volume of water works north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated. At 3.0 feet, Water
approaches or may enter lowest homes on or near Wildhog Road and
nearby canals. Flooding reaches the parking lot of the Juno Trail
Apartments. Flooding on portions of Alligator Road and Holiday
Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue Creek are flooded. Roads at
Astor Landing Campground and Lake Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood.
Water enters lower homes closest to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EST Tuesday the stage was 2.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EST Tuesday was 2.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise slightly to 3 feet late
this week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.

at 8:15 AM EST Tuesday was 17.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to continue rising, cresting at
17.2 feet this weekend.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
